jobs.title: Entry-level Consultant (2027)
jobs.description: Oliver Wyman's HK office has a strong financial-services, risk and strategy franchise. Of the big consultancies it is the one most used to non-Chinese-speaking analysts on cross-border FS work.
jobs.fit: Best consulting bet on this list: FS depth suits your VC exposure, and OW's HK intake historically includes non-Chinese speakers. Confirm 2027 intake is live before treating the deadline as real.
jobs.deadline: Check live posting — do not assume a date
steps: Open Oliver Wyman careers search.
Location → Hong Kong.
Keywords: “2027”, “Consultant”, “graduate”, or “entry”.
Open the Class of 2027 / entry-level Consultant posting.
Read eligibility (graduation year, languages) then Apply.
Screenshot the deadline — OW HK has posted hard dates before.
jobs.portalTips: OW sometimes lists Marsh McLennan group portals. Stay on Oliver Wyman / consulting graduate roles, not MMC insurance ops. Taikoo Place = Hong Kong office.
jobs.deadlineNote: A prior HK Class of 2027 posting cited ~20 Sep 2026 — always re-confirm on the live page before you plan around it.

jobs.title: Research Analyst / Associate (Asia)
jobs.description: Political risk shop advising corporates and investors on geopolitics, elections, and policy. Analysts write briefings, brief clients, and track Asia political developments.
jobs.fit: Closest to your IR/political-risk interests, but Eurasia's Asia analyst seats are few, usually Singapore or Tokyo, and rarely sponsor a fresh grad. Treat as a mentor-intro target, not an application.
steps: Open Eurasia Group Careers.
Scan open roles for Research Analyst / Associate covering Asia.
If listed by city, prefer Hong Kong / Singapore / Asia.
Read the JD for language + regional coverage (China, SEA, etc.).
Apply with a tight writing sample if requested (briefing-style).
No live Asia role? Use the general applications / contact path and note Asia interest.
jobs.portalTips: Political-risk shops hire thinly and roll openings. Check monthly. Emphasize Asia IR coursework + crisp writing over generic consulting jargon.
jobs.deadlineNote: Truly rolling — apply when a fit appears; don’t wait for a “campus season”.

jobs.title: Analyst — Political & Security Risk (Asia)
jobs.description: Global risk consultancy covering political, security, and integrity risk. HK analysts support clients with country risk, investigations support, and diligence across Greater China / SEA.
jobs.fit: Political and security risk analysis is your subject. HK is Control Risks' North Asia hub; junior analyst hires are rolling and ad hoc, so a warm intro matters more than the portal.
steps: Open Control Risks Careers.
Search or filter Location → Hong Kong / Asia Pacific.
Keywords: “Analyst”, “political”, “security risk”, “research”.
Open Analyst-level roles (not Consultant / Director).
Apply through their portal; tailor CV to risk research + languages.
Set a saved search / alert for Hong Kong Analyst roles.
jobs.portalTips: Titles mix “Analyst”, “Associate”, and practice names (Political Risk, Security, Integrity). Skip senior consulting grades. HK is a real hub — location filter matters.
jobs.deadlineNote: Rolling hiring against client demand — weak campus rhythm compared with MBB.

jobs.title: Analyst / Research Associate (Asia)
jobs.description: Independent advisory firm producing geopolitical and economic analysis for governments and corporates. Roles emphasize crisp writing and judgment under uncertainty.
jobs.fit: Writing-sample driven, remote-friendly, thin HK presence. Good for the mentor list and for getting bylines; unlikely to be the visa sponsor.
steps: Open Oxford Analytica Careers.
Review current vacancies for Analyst / Research Associate.
Check location notes (Oxford / remote / Asia coverage).
Prepare a short writing sample (1–2 pages, briefing tone).
Apply as directed; mention Asia IR focus + languages in the cover note.
If no vacancy, look for speculative / mailing-list options on the same page.
jobs.portalTips: Small firm — few postings, high writing bar. “Asia” may mean coverage from Oxford rather than an HK desk; confirm location in the JD before you assume Hong Kong.
jobs.deadlineNote: Openings are infrequent; treat the careers page as a monthly check, not a campus portal.

jobs.title: Business Analyst
jobs.description: Entry-level client-facing role advising corporates and institutions across Greater China on strategy, operations, and transformation. Strong analytical apprenticeship with global firm training.
jobs.fit: Long shot for the HK office without Chinese — HK BA intakes draw heavily on HK and Mainland universities and client work is in Chinese. Realistic path: apply to London or Amsterdam, then ask about an HK transfer after 2 years.
jobs.deadline: Class of 2027 dates vary by office — confirm live
steps: Open McKinsey’s job search (link below).
Filter Location → Hong Kong (or Greater China).
Search “Business Analyst” or “BA” + “2027”.
Open the BA / early-career posting and check eligibility (degree year).
Create / sign in to a McKinsey careers account, then Start application.
Save the posting ID — campus deadlines move; confirm before you draft.
jobs.portalTips: McKinsey’s portal often lists office + role separately. If HK BA isn’t live yet, set a job alert for “Business Analyst” + Hong Kong and check campus recruiting pages for St Andrews / UK timelines.
jobs.deadlineNote: Class of 2027 BA apps for Asia often open mid-year — confirm live dates; don’t rely on last year’s calendar.

jobs.title: Associate (Undergraduate / Master’s)
jobs.description: BCG’s Hong Kong office hires early-career Associates for strategy and transformation projects across Asia. Expect team-based problem solving, research, and client presentations.
jobs.fit: Same as McKinsey: HK office is Chinese-language client work. Apply London/Amsterdam and use HK as a later transfer, unless a specific HK posting says otherwise.
steps: Go to BCG Careers search results (link below).
Set Location filter to Hong Kong / China / Asia Pacific.
Keywords: “Associate”, “undergraduate”, or “2027”.
Open early-career / Associate postings for HK.
Apply via the BCG portal (CV + cover / online form).
If nothing shows, check “Students & Graduates” and set an alert.
jobs.portalTips: BCG splits experienced hire vs students. Use Students & Graduates paths when available. “Associate” is the undergrad/master’s title in many Asia offices — not “Business Analyst”.
jobs.deadlineNote: Greater China campus deadlines are often earlier than US — check the posting month by month.

jobs.title: Markets Analyst / Global Research (Asia)
jobs.description: Graduate entry into markets or research covering Asia equities, rates, or economics. Training programme plus desk placement in HK.
jobs.fit: Bank grad schemes are the most reliable visa sponsors in HK, but HK markets and research seats mostly ask for Mandarin. Worth one application; do not build the plan around it.
steps: Open J.P. Morgan Students & Programs.
Filter region → Asia Pacific / Hong Kong.
Browse Markets, Research, or Analyst graduate programmes.
Open the programme page and note eligibility + deadline.
Apply in the student portal; select location preferences carefully.
Track status in the same portal (assessments often follow).
jobs.portalTips: JPMorgan’s student hub is the right door — not the experienced-hire job board. Programme titles rotate (Markets, Global Research, etc.); match “Analyst” + APAC rather than hunting one fixed job ID.
jobs.deadlineNote: Deadlines differ by programme and region — read the specific APAC posting, not the US MBA calendar.
jobs.languageReq: Mandarin preferred for most HK seats

jobs.title: APAC Graduate Programme (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: BNP is the largest European bank in HK with a structured APAC graduate intake across corporate banking, markets and functions. Big European client franchise run in English and French.
jobs.fit: French firms in HK are the bloc where your languages actually count. BNP's graduate scheme is a proven visa sponsor and its HK client base is international, so no-Chinese is less of a blocker than at US banks.
jobs.deadline: Graduate programmes typically open Sep–Nov for the following summer — confirm on the live posting
steps: Open BNP Paribas careers and choose Students & Graduates.
Filter region → Asia Pacific → Hong Kong.
Search 'graduate programme 2027'; note which streams (CIB, functions) are open.
Apply early — intakes close on a rolling basis once filled.
jobs.portalTips: Mention French on page one of the CV. BNP APAC HR reads it as a fit signal for the European client desk.
jobs.deadlineNote: Confirm 2027 intake dates on the live posting; last year's calendar is not reliable.

jobs.title: V.I.E. placement — Hong Kong
jobs.description: The French V.I.E. scheme places EU/EEA nationals aged 18–28 in French companies abroad for 12–24 months, with Business France handling the visa and status. SocGen, BNP, Crédit Agricole CIB, AXA, LVMH and others post HK V.I.E. roles.
jobs.fit: Potentially the single best route on this list if you hold an EU passport: it sidesteps HK employer sponsorship entirely and the employer takes the visa risk. Verify eligibility (nationality, age, French requirement varies by posting) before anything else.
steps: Create an account on the Business France V.I.E. portal.
Filter country → Hong Kong; sector → banking/finance or consulting.
Read each posting's language requirement — some need fluent French, many only working French.
Apply directly; the company interviews, Business France handles the paperwork.
jobs.portalTips: V.I.E. postings are short and specific. Save a search and check weekly — they close fast.
jobs.deadlineNote: Rolling. Eligibility to confirm: EU/EEA nationality and under 28 at start.

jobs.title: Global Graduate Programme (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: HSBC's HK graduate programmes run across commercial banking, global banking & markets, wealth and corporate functions. The largest structured grad intake in HK.
jobs.fit: The most reliable visa sponsor in the city. Non-Chinese speakers get placed, mostly in global banking and functions rather than local commercial banking. Apply to the international-client streams.
jobs.deadline: Typically opens Aug–Sep, closes Oct–Nov — confirm live
steps: Open HSBC students & graduates.
Choose Hong Kong as location and 2027 as start year.
Read stream descriptions and pick two at most.
Complete online assessments promptly — the queue is long.
jobs.portalTips: HSBC uses a strict online-assessment funnel. Do practice tests before applying.
jobs.deadlineNote: Autumn 2026 deadline for summer 2027 start is likely — verify.

jobs.title: International Graduate Programme (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: StanChart's HK intake covers corporate & investment banking, wealth, and functions. Explicitly international rotations.
jobs.fit: Same logic as HSBC: proven sponsor, international streams, English-first. The two bank grad schemes together are the safety net under the rest of this list.
steps: Open the graduates page.
Select Hong Kong and the 2027 cohort.
Choose one business stream and one functions stream.
Apply and complete assessments within a week.
jobs.portalTips: Their application asks 'why this market' — have a real HK answer, not a generic one.

jobs.title: Management Trainee Programme
jobs.description: Swire's flagship trainee programme rotates through Cathay, Swire Properties, beverages and trading over three years. Highly competitive, English-language, historically international in intake.
jobs.fit: Classic HK route for non-Chinese-speaking graduates from UK universities; Swire has a long history of hiring exactly this profile. Sponsorship is standard for trainees.
jobs.deadline: Typically opens Sep, closes Oct–Nov — confirm live
steps: Go to Swire's careers section and find the Management Trainee programme.
Check eligibility (graduation year, mobility).
Apply once — one application covers the group.
Prepare for multi-stage assessment centres.
jobs.portalTips: They prize evidence of leadership and mobility. Ski-school instructing and the Netherlands stint both read well here.

jobs.title: Executive Trainee Programme
jobs.description: Jardines' trainee scheme rotates across the group's Asian businesses. English-language, international cohort.
jobs.fit: Second of the two big HK conglomerate schemes; same fit logic as Swire. Apply to both.
steps: Open Jardines careers.
Find the Executive Trainee programme and its 2027 dates.
Apply; expect video interview then assessment centre.
jobs.portalTips: Read their annual report first — interviews test whether you know what the group actually owns.

jobs.title: Executive (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: Financial and political communications advisory; HK office handles cross-border M&A, IPO and crisis work for Asian and Western clients.
jobs.fit: Strategic comms is where IR graduates who write well end up. Brunswick hires juniors ad hoc and values European-language coverage for Continental clients. Strong mentor-intro target.
steps: Open Brunswick careers.
Filter by Hong Kong.
If nothing junior is open, submit a speculative application with a writing sample.
jobs.portalTips: Send two published pieces (Foreign Affairs Review, New Annales). They hire on writing.

jobs.title: Analyst / Associate (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: CEO advisory, strategic comms and geopolitical risk. HK is one of its Asia hubs.
jobs.fit: Overlaps your political-risk interest with a firm that actually has HK junior seats. Intro-driven hiring.
steps: Open Teneo careers.
Filter Hong Kong.
Apply or send a speculative note via the mentor.
jobs.portalTips: Their geopolitics practice publishes; cite something specific.

jobs.title: Associate (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: Financial and public-affairs communications, strong in Asia capital-markets work.
jobs.fit: Third of the comms-advisory trio. Apply to all three; the market is small and moves by referral.
steps: Open FGS Global's site and go to careers.
Filter Hong Kong.
Apply with a writing sample.
jobs.portalTips: Same writing-sample logic as Brunswick.

jobs.title: Research Associate / Fellow (trade policy)
jobs.description: HK-based foundation focused on sustainable global trade; runs research, fellowships and a trade-policy programme.
jobs.fit: Closest thing in HK to a think-tank seat in your subject. Small team, occasional junior openings, and a fellowship route worth knowing about.
steps: Open the Hinrich site and find Careers or Programmes.
Check for research associate openings and fellowship windows.
Apply with a trade-related writing sample.
jobs.portalTips: A published piece on trade or supply chains would materially help.

jobs.title: Programme / Policy Assistant
jobs.description: Cultural and policy institution in Admiralty running programmes on Asia policy, business and arts.
jobs.fit: Fits the development/foreign-policy side and the Craft House arts work. Junior roles exist; sponsorship is the weak point.
steps: Open the Asia Society HK site.
Find Careers / Opportunities.
Apply to programme or policy roles.
jobs.portalTips: Nonprofits in HK rarely sponsor; pair this with a Working Holiday visa if eligible.

jobs.company: French Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong
jobs.title: Project / Business Development Officer
jobs.description: The largest French chamber in Asia; runs events, committees and a business-support service for French companies entering HK. Junior officers often move on to member firms.
jobs.fit: Not the destination job — the on-ramp. Everyone at BNP, AXA and LVMH HK knows the chamber; a year here is a network. French required.
steps: Open the chamber site.
Find Jobs / Careers (chamber roles and member-company roles are often listed).
Apply to chamber roles; browse member listings weekly.
jobs.portalTips: The chamber's own job board lists member-company openings — a source for the scanner too.

jobs.company: Dutch Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong / NL Consulate
jobs.title: Junior roles and member-company listings
jobs.description: Smaller than the French chamber but the natural hub for ING, ABN AMRO, Philips, Shell and Unilever people in HK. The consulate and the Netherlands investment agency also take junior policy/trade staff.
jobs.fit: Dutch-native is a real differentiator here and almost nowhere else in HK. Also the place to ask about the Netherlands–HK Working Holiday Scheme.
steps: Open the chamber site and its vacancies/jobs page.
Note member-company openings.
Email the chamber directly about junior roles — it is small enough that this works.
jobs.portalTips: Ask the consulate's economic section about junior trade-officer or policy roles.

jobs.title: Analyst — strategy, policy, research (digital assets)
jobs.description: HK has positioned itself as a licensed digital-assets hub; the larger players run policy, research and strategy teams that hire junior generalists.
jobs.fit: Your VC internship (market maps, memo, the 'Fintern' agent) is directly relevant, and these firms are English-first and sponsor. Gareth's network is strongest here — intro target.
steps: Check careers pages for HashKey, Animoca and OSL.
Search 'analyst' + 'strategy' or 'policy'.
Ask Gareth for the intro before applying cold.
jobs.portalTips: Lead with the investment memo and market maps.

jobs.title: Future Leaders Programme (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: Unilever's global graduate scheme, rotational across marketing, supply chain and customer development. Hong Kong runs a local intake in some years; the APAC hub is Singapore.
jobs.fit: Dutch-native at a Dutch company is a real signal, and UFLP sponsors as standard. Confirm HK is running a 2027 intake before applying — if not, the Singapore or UK intake with an Asia rotation is the honest alternative.
jobs.deadline: Typically autumn — confirm HK intake is live
steps: Open Unilever careers and find Future Leaders Programme.
Check which markets list a 2027 intake; look for Hong Kong.
Apply to one function stream; the process is games-based then video.
jobs.portalTips: If HK isn't listed, apply Singapore and say HK/Greater China is where you want to be.
jobs.deadlineNote: Confirm live — HK intake is not guaranteed every year.

jobs.title: Management Trainee (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: L'Oréal HK is a large office with an established management-trainee scheme across marketing, commercial and finance.
jobs.fit: French employer, big HK presence, structured sponsorship, French a plus. The most reliable consumer-goods bet on this list.
steps: Open L'Oréal careers.
Filter Hong Kong and early careers / management trainee.
Apply; expect a business-case round.
jobs.portalTips: Lead with the World Connect data work and the VC market maps — they hire for commercial analysis.

jobs.title: Graduate or trainee — corporate, strategy, retail ops (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: Both luxury groups run HK as a regional hub with corporate and brand-level junior roles. LVMH also lists HK V.I.E. placements.
jobs.fit: French/Swiss employers in a sector where HK is a real hub and Chinese is not required for corporate roles. French is a genuine asset. Check the V.I.E. portal for LVMH HK too.
steps: Open LVMH talents / Richemont careers.
Filter Hong Kong and early careers.
Cross-check the V.I.E. portal for the same groups.
jobs.portalTips: Brand-level roles (Hermès, Cartier) are listed separately from group roles — search both.

jobs.title: Graduate programme or junior analyst (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: Both spirits groups run HK as a Greater China / travel-retail hub with junior commercial and strategy roles.
jobs.fit: European employers, English-first commercial teams, sponsorship standard. Pernod is French — French a plus.
steps: Open each group's careers page.
Filter Hong Kong / Greater China.
Apply to graduate or commercial analyst roles.
jobs.portalTips: Diageo's HK roles sometimes sit under 'Asia Pacific' — widen the location filter.

jobs.title: Graduate / management trainee (Hong Kong)
jobs.description: Both run HK trainee intakes for marketing, sales and supply chain. P&G's HK office is smaller than its Guangzhou hub.
jobs.fit: Reliable sponsors with structured schemes. Weaker language fit than the French firms; apply as breadth.
steps: Open Nestlé and P&G careers.
Filter Hong Kong, early careers.
Skip any role listing Cantonese as required.
jobs.portalTips: Marketing and supply-chain streams are more often English-only than sales.
jobs.languageReq: varies — some HK sales roles ask for Cantonese

jobs.title: Graduate programme — APAC hub (Singapore)
jobs.description: The Dutch multinationals run APAC out of Singapore, not Hong Kong. Structured graduate intakes with Asia rotations.
jobs.fit: Where a Dutch-native profile carries most weight in the region. Singapore is second choice, so apply here only for the schemes that don't run an HK intake. Visa note: fresh-grad Employment Pass has a salary floor that most grad schemes clear; the UK/US passports also open Singapore's Work Holiday Programme (ages 18–25, six months) as a bridge — verify current rules.
steps: Check each company's careers page for a Singapore 2027 graduate intake.
Apply only where HK isn't offered.
State HK/Greater China as preferred rotation.
jobs.portalTips: Say 'Dutch national' explicitly; regional HR notices.

jobs.title: Research Officer / Research Associate
jobs.description: Singapore's leading Southeast Asia policy institute; junior research officer roles support programmes on regional politics, economics and security.
jobs.fit: The best pure-IR seat in the region for a fresh graduate. Publishing record and a writing sample matter; a good mentor-intro target too.
steps: Open ISEAS careers.
Look for research officer or programme roles.
Apply with a Southeast Asia–focused writing sample.
jobs.portalTips: Write something on Southeast Asian politics for the Foreign Affairs Review first.

jobs.company: UNDP Bangkok Regional Hub / The Asia Foundation / ADB (Manila)
jobs.title: Junior programme, research or policy roles
jobs.description: The regional development institutions sit in Bangkok and Manila. Entry is usually via internships, junior consultancies or programme-assistant roles rather than grad schemes.
jobs.fit: Fits the international-development interest and the World Connect / United Way work directly. Third-choice geography, so keep to strong-fit roles only; visas are handled by the institution.
steps: Check UNDP jobs, The Asia Foundation careers and ADB careers.
Filter Bangkok / Manila / regional and junior levels.
Apply where the role is explicitly entry-level.
jobs.portalTips: UN roles ask for a second UN language — French counts.

jobs.title: Research Assistant / Programme Coordinator
jobs.description: The UK's leading international-affairs institute. Junior research and programme roles across Asia-Pacific, Europe, Africa and Global Economy programmes.
jobs.fit: Your subject, in the building where it's done. Roles are few and competitive; a published piece and a mentor intro both matter. British passport means no visa question.
steps: Open Chatham House careers.
Filter to research and programme roles.
Apply with a writing sample on a regional topic.
jobs.portalTips: Research assistant roles often ask for a language; French counts.

jobs.title: Research Analyst / Research Assistant
jobs.description: The two London defence and security institutes. Junior analyst roles support regional programmes and data projects.
jobs.fit: Political and security risk without the corporate wrapper. RUSI in particular hires recent graduates as research assistants.
steps: Check both institutes' careers pages.
Look for research assistant or project roles.
Apply with a security-themed writing sample.
jobs.portalTips: RUSI's careers page lists openings under Vacancies; IISS under About us.

jobs.title: Analyst — Global Risk Analysis
jobs.description: The London HQ runs the largest political-risk analysis team in the firm. Structured analyst intake plus rolling hires.
jobs.fit: Same firm as the HK entry but London is the head office and hires more juniors. Apply here even if HK is the goal; internal moves to Asia happen.
jobs.deadline: Analyst intake typically opens autumn — confirm
steps: Open Control Risks careers.
Filter London and analyst level.
Apply; the process includes a written analysis test.
jobs.portalTips: Say explicitly that you'd relocate to Asia — it's a differentiator for London hires.

jobs.title: Consultant (2027 intake)
jobs.description: OW's largest office. Full graduate intake across financial services, public sector and strategy.
jobs.fit: The realistic route to the HK office is two years in London first. Apply London, state HK as a mobility preference.
jobs.deadline: Typically opens Sep, closes Oct–Nov — confirm
steps: Open OW careers.
Filter London, entry level, 2027.
Apply early — rolling review.
jobs.portalTips: Their application asks for office preferences; list London first, Hong Kong second.

jobs.title: Business Analyst / Associate (London, 2027)
jobs.description: The three strategy firms' London offices, the largest intakes in Europe.
jobs.fit: Where the HK versions of these roles said 'apply London', this is that entry. Standard MBB case process; IR is a common background here.
steps: Apply to each separately.
Filter London, undergraduate, 2027 start.
Book case-practice sessions through St Andrews consulting society.
jobs.portalTips: All three run campus events at St Andrews in October; attend.

jobs.company: UK Civil Service Fast Stream — Diplomatic & Development
jobs.title: Fast Streamer (Diplomatic and Development)
jobs.description: The UK government's graduate scheme; the Diplomatic and Development stream places graduates in the FCDO with overseas postings later.
jobs.fit: The most direct foreign-policy career route on any of these lists. British passport required — you have it. Long process (opens autumn, offers spring).
jobs.deadline: Typically opens late Sep, closes Oct — confirm
steps: Open faststream.gov.uk.
Register when applications open.
Complete online tests within the window; they close hard.
jobs.portalTips: Nationality and residency rules apply — check the eligibility page before spending time.

jobs.title: Executive / Associate (London)
jobs.description: The three strategic-communications firms' London head offices; largest junior intakes in the group.
jobs.fit: Same logic as the HK entries, with more seats. Brunswick runs a structured graduate programme in London.
jobs.deadline: Brunswick graduate scheme typically autumn — confirm
steps: Check Brunswick's graduate programme page first.
Then Teneo and FGS London careers.
Apply with two published pieces.
jobs.portalTips: Brunswick's programme asks for a written exercise; your Foreign Affairs Review work is the prep.

jobs.title: Global Graduate Programme (London)
jobs.description: Both banks' London graduate intakes. Same programmes as HK, applied from the UK.
jobs.fit: Apply London as the fallback to the HK application to the same scheme — the banks allow one application per cycle, so pick the office deliberately.
steps: Decide HK or London per bank before applying — one application each.
Apply to the international or global banking streams.
jobs.portalTips: Both banks' schemes include international rotations; say Asia.
jobs.deadlineNote: Confirm; one application per bank per cycle.

jobs.title: Junior Researcher / Research Assistant
jobs.description: The Netherlands' two foreign-policy and security institutes, both in The Hague. Junior researcher and trainee roles.
jobs.fit: Dutch-native and an IR degree from a UK university is exactly their junior profile. The Hague is the international-law and policy capital; roles are few but fit is high.
steps: Check both institutes' vacancy pages.
Apply in Dutch where the posting is in Dutch.
Send a writing sample on a European or Asian topic.
jobs.portalTips: Clingendael also runs a traineeship — check timing.

jobs.title: Rijkstraineeship / BZ traineeship
jobs.description: The Dutch civil-service graduate scheme and the foreign ministry's own trainee route. Dutch nationality required.
jobs.fit: The Dutch equivalent of the Fast Stream. You qualify on nationality; the process is in Dutch. Strongest pure foreign-policy route on the NL list.
jobs.deadline: Rijkstraineeship rounds typically twice a year — confirm
steps: Open werkenvoornederland.nl and search Rijkstraineeship.
Check the BZ traineeship separately on the ministry site.
Apply in Dutch.
jobs.portalTips: Two intake rounds a year; the spring round matters for a summer 2027 start.

jobs.title: Graduate / Traineeship (Amsterdam)
jobs.description: The three Dutch banks' Amsterdam traineeships. English-language working environments, Dutch a plus.
jobs.fit: The Amsterdam version of the HK bank-scheme safety net. ING's international talent programme has Asia rotations, which keeps HK in play.
jobs.deadline: Typically Sep–Nov for the following year — confirm
steps: Check each bank's traineeship page.
Apply to one stream each.
Note ING's international programme separately.
jobs.portalTips: ING explicitly recruits international profiles for the Amsterdam intake; Dutch-native with a UK degree is a strong combination.

jobs.title: Graduate programme (Rotterdam / Amsterdam / The Hague)
jobs.description: The Dutch multinationals' home-market graduate intakes. Rotational, English-first, with Asia postings later.
jobs.fit: Where a Dutch-native profile carries most weight anywhere. Apply here rather than the HK or Singapore intakes for the same companies unless HK is explicitly listed.
steps: Check each company's Netherlands graduate page.
Apply once per company; state Asia as a rotation preference.
jobs.portalTips: Unilever's Future Leaders Programme NL intake is the most structured of the four.

jobs.title: Junior consultant / analyst (Amsterdam)
jobs.description: Amsterdam offices of the comms and risk consultancies. Smaller than London; hires are ad hoc.
jobs.fit: Breadth entry. Dutch-native is a genuine differentiator for public-affairs work here.
steps: Check careers pages; filter Amsterdam.
Send speculative applications with a writing sample where nothing is open.
jobs.portalTips: Public-affairs roles in Amsterdam almost always want Dutch; you clear that.

jobs.title: V.I.E. placements from Paris-based companies (worldwide, incl. Hong Kong and Singapore)
jobs.description: French companies post V.I.E. roles abroad through Business France. As an EU national under 28 you can be placed anywhere they operate, including Hong Kong.
jobs.fit: The single strongest route across all three lists: a French company sends you to Asia and carries the visa. Filter the portal by destination, not by Paris. Working French usually sufficient.
steps: Create an account on the V.I.E. portal.
Save searches for Hong Kong and Singapore across finance, luxury and consulting.
Apply directly; the company interviews.
jobs.portalTips: Postings close fast. Weekly check is the minimum.

jobs.title: Assistant de recherche / Chargé d'études
jobs.description: Paris's foreign-policy institutes. Junior research roles, mostly in French.
jobs.fit: Fit on subject; French at working level is the constraint — postings usually want fluent written French. Realistic as a second-year target once French improves, or now with an intro.
steps: Check each institute's careers / recrutement page.
Apply in French with a French writing sample.
jobs.portalTips: Many roles are listed as 'stage' (internship) even for graduates; a paid stage is a normal entry point in France.

jobs.company: BNP Paribas / Société Générale / Crédit Agricole CIB
jobs.title: Graduate programme (Paris)
jobs.description: The French banks' home-market graduate intakes; the same firms as the HK V.I.E. and BNP APAC entries.
jobs.fit: Apply Paris only if the HK or V.I.E. route doesn't land — one application per bank per cycle. Paris programmes lead to Asia postings through the V.I.E. anyway.
steps: Decide HK vs Paris per bank before applying.
Check whether the Paris programme explicitly includes an international V.I.E. year.
jobs.portalTips: SocGen's graduate programme includes a V.I.E. year abroad as standard — worth checking.

jobs.title: Graduate / management trainee (Paris)
jobs.description: The luxury and beauty groups' Paris headquarters intakes, with Asia rotations in most programmes.
jobs.fit: Same companies as the HK list, applied at HQ. French working level is usually fine for HQ graduate schemes; Asia rotations are common and often go to people who ask.
jobs.deadline: Typically autumn / spring — confirm per group
steps: Check each group's early-careers page.
Apply once per group; list Hong Kong or Singapore as a rotation preference.
jobs.portalTips: L'Oréal's Paris management trainee scheme explicitly places trainees in Asia.

jobs.title: Junior Professional / Young Associate / Internship
jobs.description: Paris hosts the OECD, UNESCO and several other IOs. Entry is via young-professional programmes and paid internships, in English and French.
jobs.fit: International development and policy, in English, with French as the second language they actually want. The OECD Young Associates programme takes recent graduates for two years.
jobs.deadline: OECD Young Associates typically opens in spring — confirm
steps: Check the OECD careers page for Young Associates and internships.
Check UNESCO careers separately.
Apply in English; note French and Dutch.
jobs.portalTips: IO recruitment is slow; apply six months ahead of when you'd want to start.
